title: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Voice-Agent Evaluation: Reliability, Calibration, and Human Oversight
abstract: arXiv:2608.24314v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluating conversational voice agents at scale re- quires reliable assessment methods that capture both observ- able interaction quality and the contextual judgment typically provided by human evaluators. We investigate LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation by comparing human judgments with GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 on telecom and retail voice-agent conversations, across conversational quality and safety dimensions. The same interac- tions are scored under three evaluation configurations, p0, p1, and p2, to test whether automated judgments are sensitive to the evaluation setup and whether observed patterns generalize across configurations and judge models. Beyond aggregate agreement, we examine metric-level correlations, evaluator consistency, and systematic human-LLM disagreement to identify which conver- sational attributes can be judged reliably by automation and which remain sensitive to interpretation and context. translated_title: 语音代理评估中LLM评委的基准测试：可靠性、校准与人类监督
translated_abstract: 大规模评估对话式语音代理需要可靠的评估方法，这些方法既要捕捉可观察的交互质量，也要捕捉通常由人类评估者提供的上下文判断。我们通过比较人类判断与GPT-4.1和GPT-5在电信和零售语音代理对话中的评估结果，研究了LLM作为评委的评估方式，涵盖对话质量和安全性维度。相同的交互在三种评估配置（p0、p1和p2）下进行评分，以测试自动判断是否对评估设置敏感，以及观察到的模式是否在不同配置和评委模型间具有普遍性。除了总体一致性外，我们还检查了指标级相关性、评估者一致性以及系统性的人机分歧，以识别哪些对话属性可以可靠地由自动化判断，哪些仍对解释和上下文敏感。有效的语音代理评估是一个...
tldr: 本文通过比较人类与GPT-4.1和GPT-5在多种评估配置下的判断，系统性地测试了LLM评委在语音代理评估中的可靠性、校准性及人类监督的必要性，发现自动化判断对评估设置敏感且存在人机分歧，需结合人类监督以确保有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically benchmarks LLM judges (GPT-4.1 and GPT-5) against human evaluations across multiple configurations for voice-agent assessment, revealing sensitivity to evaluation setups and human-LLM disagreements that necessitate human oversight for reliable evaluation.
